content: The issue of understocking and overstocking of antiretroviral, antituberculosis, and antimalarial medicines has been documented. The following references provide detailed insights into various aspects of health economics, costing methodologies, and programmatic evaluations related to tuberculosis (TB) and other global health interventions: 1. Kellogg WK developed a guide for creating logic models, which is available in PDF format. 2. A virtual meeting held on July 2 and 7, 2020, in London, focused on country-level economic modeling, and the meeting report is available in PDF format. 3. Vassall A, Sweeney S, Kahn J, Gomez GB, Bollinger L, Marseille E, and colleagues created a reference case for estimating the costs of global health services and interventions, which is accessible online. 4. Cunnama L, Garcia Baena I, Gomez G, Lawrence Y, Levin C, Siapka M, and others developed costing guidelines specifically for tuberculosis interventions, available in PDF format. 5. Cunnama L, Sinanovic E, Ramma L, Foster N, Berrie L, Stevens W, and colleagues discussed the use of both top-down and bottom-up costing approaches in lowand middle-income countries (LMICs) to assess the incremental costs of scaling up new technologies. This work is published in Health Economics. 6. Capeding TPJ, Dela Rosa J, Lam H, Gaviola DG, Garfin A, Hontiveros C, and others analyzed the cost of TB prevention and treatment in the Philippines in 2017, with findings published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 7. Sweeney S, Cunnama L, Laurence Y, Garcia Baena I, Kairu A, Minyewete M, and others contributed to the Value TB dataset, which provides costs per intervention and is available online. 8. Chikovani I, Shengelia N, Marjanishvili N, Gabunia T, Khonelidze I, Cunnama L, and colleagues examined the financing of national TB programs and unit costs of TB services in both public and private sectors in Georgia, with results published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 9. Kairu A, Orangi S, Oyando R, Kabia E, Nguhiu P, Ong’ang’o J, and others studied the costs of providing TB services in healthcare facilities in Kenya, with findings published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 10. Chatterjee S, Toshniwal MN, Bhide P, Sachdeva KS, Rao R, Laurence YV, and colleagues analyzed the costs of TB services in India, with their work published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 11. Minyewete M, Eyob H, Letta T, Nadew E, Assefa T, Hailu B, and others evaluated the efficiency of TB service provision in public and private health sectors in Ethiopia, with findings in press in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 12. The One Health Tool is an online resource designed to assist with health planning and budgeting. 13. The TB planning and budgeting website provides resources for global tuberculosis program economics and budgeting. 14. The Social Protection Floor website offers information on social protection systems. 15. The WHO knowledge-sharing platform is an online resource for disseminating health-related knowledge. 16. Guidance for reviews of tuberculosis programs is forthcoming from the World Health Organization in Geneva. These references collectively provide a comprehensive understanding of the economic and programmatic aspects of TB and other global health interventions, emphasizing the importance of accurate costing, efficient resource allocation, and evidence-based decision-making in healthcare systems.
